results.title: Bizarre!
results.text: Interesting history of the Living Goddess but a bit creepy when you see a six year old done up like a dogs dinner!  However it does give the less fortunate girls from poor families a chance to be spoilt.

results.title: Rare Hindu Temple
results.text: One of the oldest Shiva temples dating back to the Mahabharta days. Being managed very well. However, the local pandits are bit of trouble but still one can easily manage. Four sides entry with different purposes of visit and fulfilment is a unique feature of the place. Gold and silver work in the walls and top of the temple also makes this temple unique. One can witness all types of Hindu saints here. Temple is situated on the banks of holy Bhagmati river.

results.title: Religious place
results.text: It is a religious place, nice old structure. It is near the airport. The oldest temple of Lord Shiva. The place of worship. Must visit this place if you are visiting Kathmandu. Adjacent to this temple, there is a cremation ground also.

results.title: Culture shock
results.text: As a westerner it was a bit of a culture shock to see bodies being prepared for cremation and seeing the actual cremation outside the temple.  As a non Hindu I was not permitted inside the temple but I had a guide for ten U.S. Dollars  who give me an hour tour of the temple grounds including an unobstructed view of the cremations  with excellent explanation of the customs and practices.  The guides definitely make the visit more memorable.

results.title: Amazing
results.text: No words to express this experience.  Breath taking!

results.title: Facinating
results.text: Quite strange watching funerals taking place, up to 40 a day sometimes. Get a guide to show you around and explain what is happening

results.title: A cultural reality
results.text: Pashupatinath is no particularly pretty, in fact it's almost grim. It's crowded with locals who go to hang out there and you will see lots of Hindu holymen (baba) encouraging you to photograph them for a small sum (ironically). However, it was probably my favorite of the so-called tourist spots in Kathmandu mainly for it's humanity and reality. I saw my first dead body (2 actually) in a hindu cremation ceremony. I have a decent knowledge of buddhism, christianity and Islam but have never before witnessed any Hindu ceremonies, so it was a revelation of sorts. I visited Pashupati on my second full day in Nepal, so it was also somewhat of a culture shock, in a good way, it was exotic and fascinating. Because of the spiritual element it is not inundated with tourists taking photos and you have more of a sense of the local. While my review may not make the place attractive to visit I thought it was amazing. There is also a deer park with lots of monkey's too, which are always fun to watch. It is ancient and the architecture is great, however if you don't like steps it's not particularly accessible on a hot day.

results.title: Not for Everyone but Everyone Should Visit
results.text: Not everyday you will see cremation but you can here. Just remember no pictures of the family and the cremation. Take your time stroll around to see the history behind the temple. Yes the river is filthy but don't let that stop you from visiting the Temple. You can visit all areas except the inside the Temple itself and the cremation area unless you are Hindu. Cows monkeys and deer are around. Don't pass on an opportunity to visit here.

results.title: Interesting Temple
results.text: This is a site where Hindus cremate their dead and fuenrals were taking place when we visited - which I found a little disconcerting as we seemed to be intruding on peoples grief.  There were cows and monkeys within the site and many small birds - as the local people provide food for the animals.

results.title: Very Religious
results.text: everybody Knows Pasupatinath Temple. Very religious and big.  Situated near Airport.  Allowed only for HINDUS.

results.title: The holy people
results.text:
In Nepal just outside of Kathmandu on the way to the airport is a temple .. Unfortunately I didn't have the chance to visit there, but my objective was to see a group of people called the Sadu .. They are holy people dressed in cloth with colored faces of different shades and styles ..
I was lucky enough to see a couple while walking through the markets of Kathmandu in Thamel and got a few photos .. For a few rupees, they will gladly stand with you and give you some blessings as well ..

results.title: Sadhus
results.text: Although you're not able to enter the main Temple if you're a Westerner,it's still worth a visit.You'll be charged 500Rs to get in but the money goes to the up keep of Pashupatinath.Once inside, you'll find many Sadhu's.Some covered in not much more than ash and others dresses in bright orange robes.Most have long dreadlocks and nearly all want you to take their photo.Be willing to pay them a small offering for their photo.That's usually all they want and in return they will give you blessings.Most speak great English and are happy for you to sit with them chatting.Spend time sat by the burning gats or in the Tilopa and Niropa caves a little further down the river.And please don't forget to pay the elderly peoples home a visit while you're there.It's worth getting a guide, they're cheap enough at a few pounds ( around 300-600 Rs ) they're very much in the know,don't rush you around and are friendly.They'll approach you as you enter through the gate.If you don't want to take a guide, just tell them 'no' and they won't bother you again.Enjoy you're time there, it's a lovely place.

results.title: The site is excellent
results.text: There is an entrance fee of 500 rupees pp but it's worth paying to see this site. Getting a guide is recommended as they tell you where you are allowed to go, and what you are looking at. Also they tell you when you can take pictures. The crematorium part was not smelling bad when we were there and we learned from our guide that there is only a bad smell when the dead bodies are old (waited for 3-4 days before burning). From here, you can walk to Boudhanath Stupa.

results.title: The Highway to Heaven
results.text: I like Pasupatinath very much, You need to read something before visiting it but it;s really worth to do it. You can see Hindu cremations overthere and meet many sadhus. This is special place where you can little think about your existance and life. NonHindu are not allowed to main shrine. Entrance fee is quite high (500 rupies) but it;s worth. Of course remember that this is place as all funeral places so you should not interup and behave correctly.

results.title: Please respect the mourning and do NOT take photos!
results.text:
I went here during a funeral rite. It was a strange feeling to sit there and watch someone's funeral, but it was at the same time somehow calm and comforting to see how family said their goodbyes and prepared the body for his journey covering it with beautiful clothes and flowers. The ceremony took hours. 

And then there were some Western tourists, shamelessly taking photos, in their tank tops and shorts. Please, have a little respect and cultural sensitivity! I felt shame to be a Westerner.

results.title: For people with a religious Bend
results.text: I went to Katmandu primarily to vist this temple and I was satisfied. Amazing place and a must visit. The place is clean and not a typical Temple where you find people asking for alms. Nice to pray and the system is streamlined as well. Take some prasad before entering and dont get duped by people trying to sell you stuff there. Its all available back once you have prayed. Enter the place before 1230 in the noon to see the main  temple.

results.title: cleaneness
results.text: The local people have to keep the area clean. They have to maintain the buildings, so that people can view them as it was 15yrs ago. In the evening couples sit all around the monuments and eating and drinking and making it dirty.

results.title: Very interesting, but perhaps a little intrusive?
results.text: Non-Hindus are not allowed in the temple, but I got a feeling we weren't welcomed even near the temple. I must say I felt uneasy seeing mourning families perform funeral rites right in front of us while toursts fill up memory cards snapping photos of their loved ones being cremated. I guess I just didn't feel comfortable making their spiritual rites a tourist trap. Also, the vendors in this area are far more aggresive than any other place in Kathmandu. I was latched on to for 30 minutes at a time by a few different vendors. I know they are trying to make a living, but the constant tugging on your clothing for attention completely distracts one from why they are there.

results.title: Very interesting experience
results.text: We went by with our guide who gave us the rundown on the temple. As soon as you walk in, you see the river and the area where the religious cremations take place. There were several taking place during our visit, and it was a culture shock to see the entire process. Once you turn away from the river and walk up a bit, you can also see the Sodu (the guys who have white faces and long dreads). They let you take pictures with them and are quite funny characters.

results.title: Nice
results.text: If you like visiting temples etc then this is a must. However its not the cleanest place. Its quite filthy in all honesty. Also you must keep in mind that there is a cremation ground here which is always busy. So if you have children may not be a good idea to go as these are quite morbid/disturbing things to see.
